current.text: He is one of four set Minnesota starters, with Edwards, McDaniels and Gobert. He is the team's only good passer and is expected to run the offense and handle the ball more than Edwards.
Experts expect his minutes to rise from 28 to 30 or more, about 32 a night.
Experts expect his usage to fall to about 28% next to Anthony Edwards. They expect more minutes to keep his assists steady or raise them.
Minnesota traded Naz Reid and Julius Randle and plays small, guard-heavy lineups with thin big man depth.
With Reid and Randle gone, he is expected to take on more of the rebounding and shots.
The newest notes say experts are not very worried about his ankles this season. He looks good in preseason and fits well with Edwards.
Experts rate him a second round player in categories, about top 20 or mid second round. In mock drafts they took him at pick 16 and said he should go before pick 20.
He is a mild target. Drafters fade him, but experts find real value at his price. One expert values him at mid 30s USD in auctions and bought him for 30 USD.
With a March 28 end, Minnesota plays 4, 2 and 4 games in our playoff weeks. The two-game week starts March 15, in the semifinal.
The two-game playoff week should drop him slightly on draft boards, mainly in close calls.
Minnesota has the league minimum of 13 back-to-backs. Experts are not worried about him sitting back-to-backs.
Minnesota should be competitive and is not expected to rest him for tanking. One expert predicts 53 wins.

durable.text: He is one of the best passers and transition players in the NBA. One expert calls him a generational passer and an underrated, elite offensive player.
He has run usage above 30 percent with a high assist rate. He takes a very high share of his shots from three and has unlimited range.
Threes and assists are his strongest categories, both far above the league pool.
His FG% is low on high volume and drags down a team's FG%. Finishing at the rim is his biggest weakness.
He rarely gets to the free throw line, so his good FT% moves a team's FT% only a little.
His turnovers are high, far worse than the league pool.
He adds rebounds and steals that most assist guards do not. He has had seasons of 6 rebounds, 8 assists and 1.8 steals.
He has a long history of ankle injuries, including impingement. Health is the biggest question about him. He has played 70 or more games twice.
Experts think his ankle fears are overblown, because many of his missed games came from Charlotte tanking.

note: Ball went for 29 USD in our league last season. Yahoo now values him at 32 USD (average cost 28.8 USD), ESPN at 50 USD, and experts call him a mid 30s USD player, so anything near 30 USD is fair value for a top 20 category talent. He fits best on punt FG% or punt TO teams, where his elite threes and assists come without his main costs (about 41% on 19 to 20 attempts, 3.2 turnovers). Early in the season, check that he plays the projected 30 to 32 minutes and how his usage and assists hold up next to Edwards. Keep in mind the two-game semifinal week starting March 15.
